lessons.title: God Is Love
lessons.theme: We can love because God first loved us

v: He who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, for God is love.
By this God’s love was revealed in us, that God has sent his only born Son into the world that we might live through him.
In this is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we also ought to love one another.
We love him, because he first loved us.

lessons.still: Rest your open hands on your knees, like an empty cup. Quietly say, “Lord, I have no love in myself. Please pour your love into me.” Then simply receive. Don't hurry to do anything for anyone else; first let yourself be filled with love.
teach: An empty cup cannot pour out water. Many people want to love others but grow drier the more they love, because they keep pouring out and are never filled. Love comes first among the nine fruits because it is the root of all the others; and the root of love is not in us but in God.

John says, “God is love.” He does not mean God is loving some of the time; he means love is God's very nature. How was this love revealed? God sent his one and only Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins. John stresses the order: “not that we loved God, but that he loved us,” and again, “We love because he first loved us.” Love always starts on God's side.

So the first step in practising love is not to grit our teeth and love harder, but to be still and receive being loved. Our mindset needs to shift from “I must love” to “I am loved, so I can love.” For someone filled with love, loving others is no longer a chore; it is the natural overflow of a full heart.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Self-ruled love is a transaction: I'll be good to you if you're good to me. Self-emptied love is an overflow: God loved me first, so I pass that love on. The fruit is the life of Christ flowing naturally out of a self-emptied person, not the product of self-cultivation. The source of love is God, and the glory goes to God.
q: Who is God? — “God is love.” How does this change your picture of God?
Who am I? — Are you often pouring yourself out to love others while seldom pausing to be filled with God's love?
How shall I respond? — How much time will you set aside today to quietly receive God's love?
lessons.jesus: At his baptism Jesus heard the Father say, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.” At that point he had not yet performed a single miracle. All of Jesus' loving service throughout his life flowed out of this assurance: he was loved by the Father.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, thank you for loving me first and sending your Son as the atoning sacrifice for my sins. I confess that there is no true love in me; so often it is only bargaining and calculation. Fill me with your love, so that my love flows from you and reaches every person around me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: First thing in the morning, pray silently: “I love because God first loved me.”
Write down three pieces of evidence that God has loved you today
For one of my 2s: turn the love you have received from God into a word of encouragement
lessons.noon: “We love him, because he first loved us.” — Lord, right now fill me first, then let it flow out.

lessons.title: What Love Really Is
lessons.theme: Love is not a feeling but the shape of Christ's life

v: Love is patient and is kind. Love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud,
doesn’t behave itself inappropriately, doesn’t seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil;
doesn’t rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth;
bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things.

lessons.still: Read these four verses slowly. Then replace every “love” with “Jesus” and read them again. Be still for a moment and let the Holy Spirit show you which line touches you most. Linger on that line and tell the Lord what you feel.
teach: People often read 1 Corinthians 13 at weddings, as though it were a romantic poem. But Paul wrote this chapter to a church torn by envy, factions and boasting about spiritual gifts. It was not written for honeymooners but for brothers and sisters in the middle of conflict.

Paul gives fifteen descriptions in one breath: two positive statements to begin, eight “nots”, one “rejoices with the truth”, and then four “all things”. Love is not only a warm feeling; it is concrete actions and choices. You will notice that nearly all eight “nots” deal with the self: love does not brag, is not proud, does not seek its own way, keeps no record of wrongs. The opposite of true love is the self-ruled life.

Try replacing “love” with “Jesus” and every line fits perfectly. Replace it with “I” and you can hardly read on. That is exactly the point: we cannot live out this kind of love by our own strength; only by letting Jesus live in us. The mindset shift: not “I must try hard to achieve these fifteen things,” but “Lord, please become this love in me.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: The eight “nots” in this passage are all portraits of the self-emptied life: not putting ourselves at the centre, not fighting for our own rights, not keeping a record of other people's wrongs. Humility is laying down power and returning to our place, and so is love: we stop acting as judge and return to the place of a servant.
q: Who is God? — When you read the passage with “Jesus” in place of “love”, what kind of Lord do you see?
Who am I? — When you read it with your own name in place of “love”, which line can you hardly get through?
How shall I respond? — In which line will you ask Jesus to live himself out in you today?
lessons.jesus: “Bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things”: this is exactly how Jesus loved Peter. Peter denied the Lord three times, yet after the resurrection Jesus asked him three times, “Do you love me?” He kept no record of wrongs; instead he restored Peter and entrusted him with feeding his sheep.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you are what love really is. I confess that my love so often seeks its own way and keeps account of others' wrongs. I cannot do this by myself. Live out in me a love that is patient and kind. Take away the bragging and pride in me, and reign in my heart. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Copy out 1 Corinthians 13:4–7 once, replacing “love” with “Jesus”
For one of my 2s: today, don't bring up any of their past mistakes
lessons.noon: “Love is patient and is kind.” — Lord, right now please become this love in me.

lessons.title: Love Your Enemies
lessons.theme: Only love that reaches our enemies shows it is the Father's love

v: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’
But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you,
that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.

lessons.still: Be still, and honestly allow the face of someone who has hurt you to come to mind. Don't suppress what you feel; tell the Lord exactly how it is. Then do just one thing: speak a simple blessing over that person, even if your heart is still reluctant.
teach: When the sun rises, it doesn't first check whether the people below are good or bad before deciding whether to shine on them. When the rain falls, it doesn't land only on the fields of the righteous. Jesus uses the most everyday scenes of nature to describe a love that is beyond nature: a love given not according to what the other deserves but according to the nature of the one who loves.

“Love your neighbour and hate your enemy” was the common view in Jesus' day. But Jesus said: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven. He doesn't mean we become God's children by loving our enemies; he means children resemble their Father. Loving our enemies is the family likeness, because this is exactly how the Father loved us when we were his enemies.

Loving our enemies does not mean condoning evil or having no boundaries, nor does it mean pretending we were not hurt. It is a choice of direction: not repaying evil for evil, leaving judgement to God, and praying for the other person's good. This is humanly impossible, and precisely because it is impossible, it shows that this fruit comes from the life of Christ and not from our own self-cultivation.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-ruled person pays back an eye for an eye and wants to be the judge, which is to take God's place. The self-emptied person leaves vengeance to God and returns to a human being's place. Pride provokes pride, and both sides lose; humility inspires humility, and is often the only key that unlocks a stalemate.
q: Who is God? — The Father makes his sun rise on the evil and the good. What kind of heart does this show you?
Who am I? — Is there an “enemy” in your heart whom you have secretly been hoping will get what they deserve?
How shall I respond? — What is the first prayer you can pray for that person today?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus was crucified, he prayed for those who mocked him and nailed him to the cross: “Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing.” He not only taught us to love our enemies; he lived it out himself in his moment of deepest agony. And we were among the very enemies he loved.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, thank you for loving me while I was still your enemy. I confess there is still resentment in my heart and I want to avenge myself. Today I hand judgement back to you, and I bless the person who hurt me. Let your love in me overcome my bitterness, and make me like a true child of yours. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Speak one specific blessing over someone who has hurt you
Write down what you want to “get even” over, and hand it to God
For one of my 2s: if the relationship is tense, pray for them first instead of arguing
lessons.noon: “And pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you” — Lord, right now I leave vengeance with you and bless them.

lessons.title: The Good Samaritan
lessons.theme: Love doesn't ask “Who is my neighbour?” but goes and becomes a neighbour

v: But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion,
came to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
Now which of these three do you think seemed to be a neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?”
He said, “He who showed mercy on him.” Then Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”

lessons.still: Imagine yourself walking on that road down to Jericho. Ask the Lord to show you who is lying “half dead” by the roadside on your path today. Wait quietly, and let the Holy Spirit lay a person or a need on your heart.
teach: Both the priest and the Levite “saw” him, and passed by on the other side. Perhaps they had good reasons: hurrying to serve at the temple, afraid of becoming ceremonially unclean, worried the robbers might still be around. We too often have good reasons not to stop: too busy, too much trouble, none of my business. Love is often defeated not by evil but by busyness.

The expert in the law asked, “Who is my neighbour?” He wanted to draw a boundary around love. But when Jesus finished the parable, he turned the question around: who became a neighbour to the man? The question moves from “Who deserves my love?” to “Whose neighbour am I willing to become?” The Samaritan saw, was moved with compassion, went to him, bandaged him, lifted him up and cared for him. Love is a chain of costly actions.

Our idea of love needs to shift from drawing lines to crossing them. Your 2s are not only the people who like you; they include the wounded by the roadside, people who may never be able to repay you. You don't need to do anything dramatic today. Just be willing to stop, go one step further, give a little more time, and let Christ's compassion reach someone through you.
lessons.light: 321 Light: People matter more than tasks. The priest and the Levite missed the person for the sake of the task; the Samaritan set the task aside and took the person to heart. The self-emptied life no longer asks, “What's in it for me?” but, “Lord, how do you want me to love this person?”
q: Who is God? — Jesus is like the Samaritan who stopped. How have you experienced him stopping for you?
Who am I? — What “good reason” do you most often use to walk past people who are hurting?
How shall I respond? — For whom are you willing to stop and go one step further today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus is the true Good Samaritan. We lay by the roadside, beaten half dead by sin, and religion and the law could only pass by. But he came to us himself, was moved with compassion, healed our wounds with his blood, and paid every cost to care for us to the very end.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for stopping for me when I was half dead, for healing me and caring for me. I confess that I often walk past people in need for the sake of busyness and convenience. Give me a heart that is moved with compassion, and let me become a neighbour to someone today. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Today, notice someone who needs help, and stop to greet them
Set aside one “too busy” task and spend that time with someone instead
For one of my 2s: give them some care that costs you something
lessons.noon: “Go and do likewise.” — Lord, right now let me stop and be a neighbour to someone.

lessons.title: Practising Love Toward My 2
lessons.theme: Love not only in word, but in deed and in truth

v: By this we know love, because he laid down his life for us. And we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers.
But whoever has the world’s goods and sees his brother in need, then closes his heart of compassion against him, how does God’s love remain in him?
My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.

lessons.still: Take out last week's “My 2 List”. Pray quietly and ask the Holy Spirit to show you the one person you are to love in a concrete way this week. Write their name on this page, then draw a small cross beside it to remember how the Lord has loved you.
teach: A letter full of “I love you” that never turns into anything will disappoint in the end; a bowl of hot soup quietly brought out late at night can say more than a thousand words. John says: let us not love only in word or with the tongue, but in deed and in truth. The fruit of love is something people can touch and taste.

John defines love from the cross: “By this we know love, because he laid down his life for us.” Then he brings that lofty truth down to the most ordinary place: seeing a brother in need and closing our hearts to him. Laying down our lives for our brothers seldom means actually dying; far more often it means giving up our time, money, pride and convenience.

This week we have looked at the source of love, the shape of love, loving our enemies and being a neighbour. Now choose one of your 2s and plan a concrete act of love: a meal, a letter, a visit, an apology that is long overdue. Love is the root of all the fruit. Next week we will see the second fruit that grows naturally out of love: joy.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your lifestyle changes; change your lifestyle and your relationships change. The fruit of love doesn't come from self-cultivation; it is Christ's self-giving love flowing out through a self-emptied person. Loving one “2” in a concrete way is building God's kingdom system here on earth.
q: Who is God? — The Lord laid down his life for us. How does this redefine what you understand by “love”?
Who am I? — Do you often say kind things to one of your 2s while seldom showing it in action?
How shall I respond? — This week, toward which 2 will you take what concrete act of love?
lessons.jesus: Jesus' love was always concrete: he touched lepers, cooked breakfast for his disciples, and from the cross entrusted his mother to John. Even in his moment of greatest pain he was thinking of other people's needs. His love never stopped at words.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you laid down your life for me, and so I know what love is. Remove the hardness that closes my heart to compassion, so that my love is not only in word and tongue but in deed and in truth. This week I want to love the 2 you have given me. Please love them yourself, through me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: For one of my 2s: complete one concrete act of love this week
For this 2, give up a block of time you had meant to keep for yourself
Write down one moment this week when you experienced the fruit of love
lessons.noon: “Let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only” — Lord, right now let your love become my action.
